name: agent-fs-per-path-permission
body:
Law (prose; assessed by review): the fs tools (`apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp`) SELF-ENFORCE per-path scope. Each tool reads the acting agent's own EFFECTIVE `permission.edit` scope — its ALLOW and DENY entries, evaluated in order with the LAST matching entry winning (a path matched by no entry is refused; deny-by-default) — and REFUSES any path not granted by them. The fs scope therefore EQUALS the agent's `edit` scope: a DENY entry the `edit` permission honours also refuses the fs operation. The rule set and the candidate path are resolved in ONE consistent frame (the same root), so a grant matches exactly the path it names; and for a code-writer a path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is refused regardless of the caller-supplied directory. The tool-level grant is only the tool's CALLABILITY gate; per-path scoping lives INSIDE the tool, never in opencode's matching of a custom tool's path argument.

Acceptance: a generated code-writer's permission block grants `apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp` deny-by-default — never a scalar `: allow`, and never a blanket `""*"": allow` — with its allow entries granted ONLY under `apg/.worktrees/*/` (WORKTREE-ONLY; the repo-root variants are not granted, per `requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only`). The worktree form is required because opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout); unlike cwd-agnostic bash command patterns they are not exempt (the agent-builder template's rule 10). The tool refuses a path outside the acting agent's granted entries AND a path whose last matching `edit` entry is a deny; a broad allow with a later sibling deny therefore refuses that sibling path, matching `edit` (the reported feedback-14 escape: an allow-only fs scope let a broad allow override a sibling `deny`). How the tool learns which agent is acting, and how the single frame is established, are implementation concerns for the plan; the enforcement — an out-of-scope, deny-revoked, or main-resolving path is refused — is what this law fixes.
